Practice Route maps connect to details, similarity, compare, favorites and relation graph
Browser-local Training Journal with finished session history and per-map completion timestamps
7-day completion KPIs, 14-day activity bars and 28-day Chart DNA exposure averages
Optional session feel and notes with JSON journal export/import
Feedback-adaptive SR band suggestion that moves conservatively from prior explicit session feedback
Recorded training sessions can restore their Practice Route configuration
Training Insights compares the latest 7, 28 or 90 days against the immediately previous equal-length period
Period KPIs for completed maps, activity days, recorded sessions and average official SR exposure
Current-versus-previous Chart DNA exposure bars plus SR-band, target-skill and explicit feel distributions
Copyable local training report that explicitly avoids performance or skill-improvement claims
Replay Failure Signals keeps imported .osr outcome records locally with accuracy, judgement mix, combo and miss summaries
Lazy 256-shard checksum lookup resolves one replay MD5 back to a Ranked beatmap without loading the whole catalogue
Browser replay parsing now exposes replay timestamp, miss rate and non-300 rate while remaining explicitly header-only
PC replay parsing adds key-input median-gap and burst-variability proxies without claiming exact miss locations
Replay records can reopen linked map details and optionally mark the matching active Practice Route map complete
Same-map Replay Trend Lab with accuracy, miss, non-300 and combo history
Mod-aware same-map filtering and same-Mod Practice Route before-after comparisons
Replay timestamp provenance separates actual replay time from import-time fallback
Repeated outcome summaries by dominant base Chart DNA axis with sample-size and mod-mix caveats
Replay Signals JSON import merges portable local histories and retries checksum resolution
Replay Profile summarizes same-map replay variability with sample SD and observed ranges
A-D data sufficiency grade uses only sample count, replay timestamp provenance, map linkage and Mods separation
Per-Mod technical statistics compare repeated outcome samples without difficulty adjustment or causal claims
Automatic replay observations appear only from repeated samples and stay descriptive rather than skill labels
Replay metric aggregation is null-safe so missing accuracy or timing values are never treated as zero
Experimental PC Timeline Alignment matches circle and slider-head timestamps to one replay keydown each on checksum-identical local maps
10-second anomaly candidate regions summarize unmatched tap heads, early/late residuals, cursor distance, local strain and overlapping stream/burst context
Alignment reports explicitly separate replay total misses from unmatched-object candidates and never claim exact judgement locations
DT, NC and HT replays are excluded from timeline alignment until clock-rate transformation is validated
Local PC server now serves Ranked UI assets and public data shards required by Replay Signals, Trends, Profile and Alignment
Local hitobject feature vectors retain x/y coordinates for optional cursor-distance alignment
Repeat Region Consensus groups supported PC alignments by exact beatmap checksum and Mods combination
Repeated 10-second anomaly candidates report recurrence, longest consecutive appearance and averaged alignment signals
Per-replay presence strips show when a region reappeared across recent alignment samples
Repeat-region thresholds support two, three or majority recurrence across the latest 5, 10 or all matching alignments
Repeat-region wording explicitly treats missing windows as absent from the saved top-candidate set rather than confirmed clean play
New PC alignments store 10-second Region Fingerprints from local .osu rhythm and geometry features
Region Fingerprints summarize density, gap variation, spacing, angle variation, slider share, fast-gap share, jump share and local strain
Structural labels include Stream/Burst, Jump, Tech/Rhythm, Slider-heavy, Dense/Reading, Flow and Mixed
Repeat Region Consensus can filter recurring anomaly candidates by structural fingerprint
Individual PC alignment candidates and exported reports include structural fingerprints with legacy fallback for older records
Fingerprint wording remains descriptive and does not treat structural classes as official difficulty types or player weaknesses
Failure Structure Profile aggregates repeated alignment candidate windows across checksum+Mods groups
Cross-map structure composition reports candidate-window counts, average recurrence, alignment score and unmatched share
Failure Structure Profile supports all-time, 30-day and 90-day scopes plus minimum alignment-group size
Structure bars link back to the matching Repeat Region structural filter
Failure Structure wording explicitly uses repeated saved anomaly candidates as its denominator instead of total play time or failure probability
M4 OSL Client moves from planned to building with a local Songs Library Bridge
Local server auto-detects common osu! stable Songs paths and supports an explicit manual path
Incremental SQLite library index reuses unchanged .osu files by mtime and size while storing metadata and MD5 locally
Local Library Search can analyze an indexed .osu directly into existing Chart X-Ray and Skill DNA without a file picker
Client scan runs in a background server thread with live scanned, updated, reused and error counters
Indexed file analysis is constrained to the configured Songs root and the server remains bound to 127.0.0.1
GitHub Pages keeps the Client UI read-only and never attempts local file-system access
Healthy Chart DNA backfill batches can target up to 2200 charts while preserving the one-request-per-second cap
Chart DNA CI time budget increases from 32 to 40 minutes only for the same capped request cadence
Method-ineligible too-short charts are marked terminal and skipped instead of being re-requested indefinitely
Ranked summary now exposes unsupported, resolved, remaining and successful-request-throughput DNA metrics
Adaptive DNA batches cool down to smaller targets when the prior run was blocked or had lower success
M4 Phase 2 adds a local Replay Inbox for actual .osr files under an auto-detected or explicitly configured replay folder
Replay Inbox is incrementally indexed in the same local SQLite database with replay timestamp, score, combo, Mods, accuracy and beatmap checksum
Replay Inbox rows join back to the active Songs library by beatmap MD5 without exposing local filesystem paths to the browser
One-click Replay Inbox analysis loads the matching local .osu when available and feeds Replay Signals plus PC Timeline Alignment
Optional tab-open replay watch rescans about every 12 seconds only while the Client tab is open and does not claim to capture every osu! play
Replay file reads are constrained to the configured replay root and replay-to-map joins are constrained to the active Songs root
M4 Phase 3 adds a bounded Background Chart DNA queue to the local OSL Client
Background DNA caches compact derived skill summaries in local SQLite without uploading local .osu files
DNA cache validity is tied to the indexed map path, MD5 and mtime so changed charts are not silently reused
Client status exposes cached and remaining DNA counts plus live processed/analyzed/error progress
Background DNA batches can process 200, 1000, 2500 or 5000 local maps and can be stopped from the Client tab
Local Library Search displays the dominant cached DNA axis and overall heuristic score when available
Opening a local map writes its derived DNA summary through to the same local cache
M4 Phase 4 adds a persistent server-side Songs and Replay watcher while OSL Client is running
Watcher settings persist in local client.json with a configurable 15 to 600 second interval
Dependency-free polling signatures trigger incremental scans only after actual .osu or .osr tree changes
Watcher state exposes last check, last detected change and automatic scan count in the Client UI
The older tab-open Replay watch yields when the server-side watcher is enabled to avoid duplicate polling
Songs path changes now preserve Replay, watcher and other local Client settings instead of overwriting client.json
Chart DNA backfill now has a push fallback trigger when the analyzer or its workflow changes
Ranked summary exposes the Chart DNA collector's own updated_at timestamp separately from metadata freshness
Chart DNA UI marks collection as delayed after three hours without a collector checkpoint
Collector health distinguishes schedule delay from source blocking and shows the latest batch success rate
M4 Phase 5 adds a local OSL Client updater with explicit check and apply controls
Updater source is pinned to the official EpicenterGUY/osu-skill-lab main branch on raw.githubusercontent.com
Only a fixed whitelist of Client shell files can be replaced and local DB/config files are excluded
Every downloaded update file is verified by expected byte size and Git blob SHA-1 before installation
Client files are backed up before replacement and partially applied updates are automatically rolled back on failure
Successful server updates require an explicit OSL Client restart; updates are never silently auto-installed
M4 Phase 6 adds a Windows installer that downloads and verifies the official Client manifest before installing
Installed Client files live under %LOCALAPPDATA%/osu-skill-lab while client.db and client.json remain under the existing user data directory
Windows Start Menu and optional desktop shortcuts launch through a single-instance Python launcher
Optional Windows login autostart runs the local Client quietly without opening duplicate server instances
The launcher records and probes the active localhost runtime so reopening OSL Client focuses the existing server instead of spawning another
Client UI exposes installed/portable state, autostart controls and a restart action for applying server updates
Standard uninstall removes program files and shortcuts while preserving local database and settings
